description: Report which parts of one GraphQL schema can no longer change without breaking somebody. The central finding is an enum reachable as both an output and an input: adding a value breaks clients that switch on it and removing one breaks callers that send it, so there is no safe change in either direction. Also reports a deprecated non-null field, which cannot be removed until a separate release makes it nullable, and counts the fields already frozen by a non-null promise. Pay 160000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

schema.description: The schema to analyse. GraphQL SDL, read as a documented subset: type, interface, union, enum, input and scalar definitions with arguments, wrappers and defaults. Type extensions and directive definitions are listed as not modelled. Nothing is fetched and no registry is consulted, so the documents supplied are the whole input.

name: graphql_audience_risk_audit

both_direction_type_count.description: Types reachable as both an input and an output, which is where evolution room disappears.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

constraints.description: Per reachable type: which directions it flows, and its counts of non-null outputs, required input fields and required arguments.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

frozen_field_count.description: Output fields carrying a non-null promise, which cannot be relaxed without affecting clients.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

stable.description: True only when no type was found to have lost its room to move. Not a judgement that the schema is well designed.

title: GraphQL Evolution Risk Audit
